system.summary: A Spanish chancery syllabary: consonant signs with vowel marks (tail a, bar e, dot or front bar i, plain o, circle u), signs for syllables and short words (que, no, yo, po, tra, pli, qua), single letters with homophones (e, n, s, r, a, y) and code groups (dinero, ducado/ducados, aqui, Sena, su Mag.d; probably armada, guerra, amigos).
system.notes: 138 kinds of sign as transcribed: many are a base with a mark, and a few are probably one sign transcribed two ways. Homophones counted as seen: a has M, ɛ, ꝶ, ─a and ꝯ; e has tt, ŧt and r; s has b, t, ȯ and b̄; n has Ω and oʒ.

prior_solution.where: Decipherments written at the time on the letters themselves (interlinear and margin). No edition or study of the cipher found: Martín Aizpuru (Onomázein 2025) studies other Pacheco letters to Granvelle (Real Biblioteca) linguistically; Van Durme 1956 (cited by the BNE record) not seen; Tomokiyo's list has no Pacheco key. Sibling letters with the same key in the Real Biblioteca (II/2251), transcribed (with their decipherments, not the cipher) by H15Corpus.

conditions.human_role: Outside contribution: Michael Brackx chose the target, set the rounds (locate the cipher and its decipherments, transcribe, align by letters then by syllables, recheck look-alike signs side by side, recheck letter 1 at full size, review) and approved each step. Transcription, key, decoder and reading were done by Claude Code under his direction.
tools: BNE Digital viewer in a browser (JPEGs taken out of the PDF and cropped)

solution.what: BNE record, Tomokiyo's list of Spanish ciphers (cached upstream), Pich-Ponce PP1-PP3, web search: no edition or key of these letters. Martín Aizpuru 2025 studies forty other Pacheco/Bolea letters to Granvelle (Real Biblioteca) linguistically; Van Durme 1956 not seen.
BNE Digital 'high' PDFs of MSS/20214/61/1-6 opened one at a time in the viewer; JPEGs taken out of the PDF and cropped.
All six letters viewed at overview size; every cipher passage found in 61/1-4 and 61/6 carries a decipherment of the time (interlinear or margin); 61/5 shows none.
Letter 1 blocks aligned with their glosses one sign per letter: fails (far fewer signs than letters).
Syllabic cipher: 'de donde' has the same signs in R2 and R4, and the sign count of each block is near the syllable count of its gloss.

Letter 2 aligned with its margin sign for sign on slope-following crops: 'yo me hallo confuso en hallarme en este tienpo tan falto de dinero'; the consonant-plus-vowel-mark structure found (ꝺꝶ ta, ꝺ̶ te, ─ꝺ ti, ꝺ̨ to; bꝶ fa, b° fu).
Letters 3 and 4 aligned with their margins (E-H, I, J, K, L, N); the same groups recur for the same words (halla, podello, dinero 3z, es verdad, necessidad, ducado 43 / ducados 43b).
Look-alike signs cropped side by side at 3-4.5x: ꝗ̶ ve / ꝗ vo, ∂ꝶ la / ∃ꝶ sa, aꝶ̶ ll / aꝶ ra split; plain ꝺ, ꝺꝶ, ʒ and ꝺ̶ not separable at the scan's resolution.
Letter 1 re-read at full size: A1 'tt Ω' en (not tt ꝺ), B1/B3 ∂ꝶ la, a 'de'-shaped sign for aqui, 6 l; a further glossed run (P1-P2) found and transcribed.

All images of the six letters viewed. Letter 3's image 2 is a second photograph of f. 1r on which the margin decipherment, faint on image 1, is legible (the Prince of Salerno at Castro, Sermoneta). The address leaves name the recipient as bishop of Arras. Letter 5 (2 June 1554) has no cipher.

Compared with the Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554 as known from vargas1552: same design (base sign plus vowel marks, short-word codes of the x-o type), no shared code group among the few known; the full table is not in the repository, so the identity is not tested.

The 56 cipher tokens left without a value aligned with their decipherments: 39 valued, several by the vowel-mark model (ɓ fo, ─ꝗ─ ve, plain ∇ ho, n g, r° du) and some as codes (gua armada, troꝶ guerra, si amigos, ros and ιos su Md, ụʒ Sena); valued share 0.94 -> 0.98.

Look-alikes re-read on side-by-side crops across letters: the yo sign (large Ʒ) and a small hooked z ɀ (do: donde ×2, acabado, donativo, haviendo, ducados) are two signs; plain ꝺ is l in 22 of 31 places; x i/y and ꝯ (h)a are one value each; D6 re-read in full (sus tramas y intelligencias), ı in A2 is a comma. Two-valued tokens 126 -> 62.

Pacheco's letters to Granvelle in the Real Biblioteca (II/2251, Naples 1554; H15Corpus marks '[mensaje cifrado]') use the same key: on f. 22r the unchanged key decodes 'y [que] ninguno' under the margin decipherment; on f. 22v ụʒ stands under the interlinear 'nueva empresa de Sena', confirming the code group valued from one BNE place.

Pacheco's thirteen letters of 1554-1555 in the Real Biblioteca (II/2251) viewed; the cipher of the four that carry it (5 and 17 Jan, Feb, 30 Mar 1554; 37 lines, 626 signs (590 when first transcribed)) transcribed in siblings/rb2251/ and aligned with the decipherments of the time (as transcribed by H15Corpus and checked on the images). The BNE key valued 86% of the signs before the reading and its decodes followed the decipherments; new values: ꝺ° tu, -d mi, dꝶ ma, ◻̇ tri, fꝶ pa; codes ιoz su Santidad, 42 duque, 36 duque de Florencia, iz cardenal, ꝗz Ingalaterra; ụʒ Sena and ιos su Mag.d confirmed. 97% of the sibling signs valued (608 of 626). Plain ꝗ as transcribed covers a que sign as well as the v sign.

Plain ꝗ compared side by side on the sibling images (3.5x): the v syllables are mostly the barred ꝗ̶, a separate sign; the plain two-storey ꝗ has the same shape where it reads que and where it reads r (H32a); a small 9-like q (lo) had also been written ꝗ. que and r not separable by shape at this resolution.
dec1554.py decodes all 62 lines with the rebuilt key without hand corrections; the decode gives the decipherment's syllables in full, in most of the passage, or in part, as graded in NOTES.md.

validation.notes: syllabary with homophones and look-alike signs: 138 sign types over 887 tokens (about 6 per type), and several signs keep two values; the letter model cannot separate the reading from a fitted key on so few tokens per type. The reading rests on the decipherments written at the time.

texts.label: Naples, 4 Apr 1554 (MSS/20214/61/1)
texts.summary: The viceroy reports on the donative, on whether the enemy fleet will come and bring war, on the need for foreign troops because the people of the kingdom cannot be trusted, and that there is no money left for the demands made on him.
texts.note: The reading is the decipherment written at the time on the letter, transcribed; the state 'read' rests on it. How far the decode with the rebuilt key gives the same syllables is graded passage by passage in NOTES.md (How it was read).

texts.note: The reading is the decipherment written at the time on the letter, transcribed; the state 'read' rests on it. How far the decode with the rebuilt key gives the same syllables is graded passage by passage in NOTES.md (How it was read).

texts.label: Naples, 15 May 1554 (MSS/20214/61/3)
texts.summary: The Prince of Salerno is still at Castro and wants to come to Sermoneta to pursue his plots. Only 2,500 ducats of annuities on the fiscal revenues have been sold at ten per cent redeemable; he would sell up to 25,000 at that price if buyers could be found, but sees no way to raise the money.
texts.note: The reading is the decipherment written at the time on the letter, transcribed; the state 'read' rests on it. How far the decode with the rebuilt key gives the same syllables is graded passage by passage in NOTES.md (How it was read).

texts.label: Naples, 24 May 1554 (MSS/20214/61/4)
texts.summary: Things in Naples are getting tighter if the Venetian ambassador's news is true; 70,000 ducats a month will now go on the war of Siena and the kingdom; the excesses of the troops should be reduced; the matter of England.

human_check.passage: d2, BNE MSS/20214/61/2, cipher lines C1-C3 (yo me hallo confuso en hallarme en este tiempo tan falto de dinero) and their margin decipherment
human_check.note: Signs counted on crops of the BNE image, strip by strip, against the transcription: 5, 10, 10 and 7, as transcribed. The repeated signs have the same shapes: ∇ꝶ aꝶ̶ (ha-ll) in hallo and hallarme, and ꝺ+ (me). ꝺ̶ (te) is crossed through and ─ꝺ (ti) has its bar in front. The margin read as far as dinero matches. One remark on notation, with no change of value: the tail of ∇ꝶ (ha) is f-like (ſ), not p-like; aꝶ̶ (ll) is a struck p. The image crops were prepared with Claude Code; the reading of the signs and of the margin was the checker's own.
